title: normalize-chatv1-param-gateway-stop-array-demultiplex-and-logprob-fallback
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: customers expect /v1/chat.completions parity for both param semantics and runtime behavior. We observed two classes of incompatibilities: 1) parameter normalization mismatch (temperature/top_p defaults, n/stream interplay, role aliasing) that produced differing tokenization & stop behavior across the OpenAI compatibility layer; 2) stop/logprobs output shape and streaming framing differences that caused downstream SDKs to mis-handle function/tool call boundaries and logprob arrays. This PR introduces a lightweight parameter gateway that normalizes incoming v1 chat params, demultiplexes mixed stop arrays into deterministic internal stop heuristics, and implements a best-effort logprob fallback strategy when tokenization or model variant mismatches occur. Summary of changes and motivation: - normalize parameters: unify temperature/top_p/default sampling, coalesce n & best_of semantics to our internal path, and preserve explicit user intent when both sampling and beam-like params are provided - role aliasing: map common role synonyms (assistant/system/user) and preserve unknown role metadata in a dedicated header to avoid dropping role-scoped instructions - stop array demultiplex: accept mixed-type stop arrays (strings, arrays, regex-like markers) and convert into two internal ordered strategies: strict-stop (exact string matches) and token-aware-stop (byte/token prefix based) so that streamed responses surface stop sentinels deterministically - logprob fallback: when requested logprobs cannot be produced due to quantized model variants or tokenization drift, include an explict fallback envelope with approximate_logprobs and a reason code rather than failing the request - streaming framing: add a small handshake/heartbeat improvement to ensure framed JSON toolcall boundaries are emitted before stream truncation on client disconnects - structured tool output: ensure function/tool outputs are wrapped in the framed-json envelope compatible with OpenAI v1 expectations and include an annotation header for partial outputs Implementation highlights: - new component api/openai_compat/param_gateway.go implements a coercive but reversible normalization layer with comprehensive unit tests - runtime/stream/stop_demux.go contains the stop demultiplexing pipeline plus a deterministic priority resolver so stop heuristics do not rely on map iteration order - runtime/output/logprob_fallback.go implements fallback envelopes and integrates with tokenization metrics to log events for downstream quality tooling - protocol/framing/framed_json.go and runtime/stream/coordinator.go updated for a short-lived handshake frame and a heartbeat for long-running streams - docs/openai_compat.md documents compatibility guarantees and the new 'compatibility-fallback' header which downstream SDKs can opt into Checklist: - [x] param gateway core logic and unit tests - [x] stop demux pipeline + integration tests using existing eval harness - [x] streaming handshake + heartbeat smoke tests - [x] docs and SDK notes - [x] manual regression testing against a curated suite of OpenAI chat vectors Backwards compatibility and rollout plan: - Default behavior maintains previous user-visible semantics except in rare ambiguous cases where we now make deterministic choices (documented in docs/openai_compat.md and flagged with Compatibility-Note header). - We will roll this as a staged feature flag: start on staging for 48h, then opt-in for canary customers, then global after 7 days of monitoring. - Metricization: added compat.gateway.* counters and compat.fallback.logprob reason tags so we can measure user impact. Related: ENG-2109 (parity spec), SUP-3492 (customer-facing incident around missing logprobs).
commits_summary: 4 commits: (1) param gateway + unit tests; (2) stop demultiplexer + integration tests; (3) logprob fallback + streaming handshake; (4) docs and test vector additions. Short SHAs: c3a1d2f (gateway), f7b4e91 (demux), a12e3cd (logprob), b9d7f02 (docs).

ci_log_summary: CI passed after two flakes retried: linting (one gofmt failure fixed), unit tests (one flaky stream test retried and stabilized). All checks green on final run.
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: param normalization gateway, deterministic stop array demultiplex, best-effort logprob fallback envelope, streaming handshake for toolcall boundaries, and docs explaining compatibility cases. Feature rolled out behind a staged feature flag; no breaking changes expected.
notes_for_release_team: Coordinate staged roll-out: enable feature flag in staging cluster on 2026-03-03 for 48h; monitor compat.gateway.* and compat.fallback.logprob telemetry; notify SDK teams (Python/TS/Go) to pull SDK-notes/openai-compat.md updates; prepare rollback plan if fallback rate >0.5% over 24h.
test_plan: Unit tests (api/openai_compat/*), integration tests (tests/compat/*), streaming handshake smoke test (tests/streaming/*), manual regression using curated OpenAI vectors. Load test with canary traffic to verify no latency regression in dedicated pods.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: behavioral changes are deterministic and documented, but there's a small risk for edge cases where mismatched tokenizers change stop placements. Mitigations: staged rollout, telemetry, and immediate rollback path.
notes: This PR intentionally prefers deterministic compatibility choices when inputs are ambiguous; follow-up work may expose finer-grained knobs per-customer if needed.
